items.stem: A solid is in the form of a cylinder with hemispherical end. The total height of the solid is 20 cm and the diameter of the cylinder is 7 cm. Find the total volume of the solid. (Use π = 22/7)
items.answer: The solid is a cylinder capped by a hemisphere at each end, so the common radius is r = 7/2 = 3.5 cm. The two hemispherical caps together take up 2r = 7 cm of the total height, so the cylinder is h = 20 − 7 = 13 cm tall. Volume of solid = volume of cylinder + 2 × volume of hemisphere = πr²h + 2 × (2/3)πr³ = πr²(h + 4r/3) = (22/7) × (7/2)² × [13 + (4/3) × (7/2)] = (77/2) × (53/3) = 4081/6 ≈ 680.2 cm³. Hence the total volume of the solid is 680.2 cm³.

items.stem: The weight of two spheres of same metal are 1 kg and 7 kg. The radius of the smaller sphere is 3 cm. The two spheres are melted to form a single big sphere. Find the diameter of the new sphere.
items.answer: The smaller sphere weighs 1 kg and has radius r = 3 cm, so its volume is V₁ = (4/3)π(3)³ = 36π cm³. Since both spheres are of the same metal, 1 kg of it occupies 36π cm³. The recast sphere weighs 1 + 7 = 8 kg, so it occupies 8 × 36π cm³. If R is its radius, (4/3)πR³ = 36 × 8π, so R³ = 36 × 8 × 3/4 = 216 = 6³, giving R = 6 cm. Hence the diameter of the new sphere is 2R = 12 cm.

items.stem: A hemispherical depression is cut from one face of a cubical block, such that diameter l of hemisphere is equal to the edge of cube. Find the surface area of the remaining solid.
items.answer: Let the edge of the cube be l, so the hemisphere carved out has radius r = l/2. Cutting the depression removes the flat circular area πr² from one face and exposes the curved hemispherical surface 2πr² in its place. Surface area of the remaining solid = surface area of cube − area of the circular base + curved surface area of hemisphere = 6l² − πr² + 2πr² = 6l² + π(l/2)² = l²(6 + π/4) = l²(6 + 22/28) = l²(6 + 11/14). Hence the surface area of the remaining solid is 95l²/14 square units.

items.stem: The internal and external diameters of a hollow hemispherical vessel are 16 cm and 12 cm respectively. If the cost of painting 1 cm² of the surface area is Rs. 5.00, find the total cost of painting the vessel all over. (Use π = 3.14)
items.answer: The worked solution takes the outer radius R = 8 cm and the inner radius r = 6 cm. Painting the vessel all over covers the outer curved surface 2πR², the inner curved surface 2πr² and the flat annular rim π(R² − r²). Total surface area = 2πR² + 2πr² + π(R² − r²) = π[2 × 64 + 2 × 36 + (64 − 36)] = π[128 + 72 + 28] = 228π = 228 × 3.14 = 715.92 cm². Cost of painting = 715.92 × 5 = Rs 3579.60. Hence the total cost of painting the vessel all over is Rs 3579.60.

items.stem: Water is flowing through a cylindrical pipe, of internal diameter 2 cm, into a cylindrical tank of base radius 40 cm, at the rate of 0.4 m/s. Determine the rise in level of water in the tank in half an hour.
items.answer: Radius of the pipe r = 2/2 = 1 cm, and the flow speed is 0.4 m/s = 40 cm/s. In one second the water leaving the pipe is a cylinder of radius 1 cm and length 40 cm, so its volume is π(1)² × 40 = 40π cm³. Half an hour is 30 × 60 = 1800 seconds, so the volume delivered is 40π × 1800 = 72000π cm³. This water spreads over the tank of radius R = 40 cm, raising the level by H, where π(40)²H = 72000π, so H = 72000/(40 × 40) = 45. Hence the level of water in the tank rises by 45 cm.

items.stem: Water is flowing at the rate of 15 km/hr through a cylindrical pipe of diameter 14 cm into a cuboidal pond which is 50 m long and 44 m wide. In what time the level of water in pond rise by 21 cm ?
items.answer: Radius of the pipe r = 14/2 = 7 cm = 7/100 m, so its cross-section is πr² = (22/7) × (7/100)² m². The water travels 15 km = 15000 m in one hour, so in t hours the volume discharged is (22/7) × (7/100)² × 15000t m³. The pond must gain 50 × 44 × (21/100) m³ of water. Equating the two, (22/7) × (7/100) × (7/100) × 15000t = 50 × 44 × (21/100), which reduces to 22 × 7 × 150t = 50 × 44 × 21, so t = (50 × 44 × 21)/(22 × 150 × 7) = 2. Hence the level in the pond rises by 21 cm in 2 hours.

items.stem: A toy is in the form of a cylinder of diameter 2√2 m and height 3.5 m surmounted by a cone whose vertical angle is 90°. Find total surface area of the toy.
items.answer: The cylinder has diameter 2√2 m, so its radius is r = √2 m, and its height is h = 3.5 m. The cone on top has vertical angle 90°, so in the right isosceles triangle formed by the two slant edges AC = BC = l and the base AB = 2√2 we have AB² = l² + l² = 2l². Thus (2√2)² = 2l², i.e. 8 = 2l² and l = 2 m. Total surface area of the toy = curved surface of cylinder + base of cylinder + curved surface of cone = 2πrh + πr² + πrl = πr(2h + r + l) = π√2(7 + √2 + 2) = π√2(9 + √2) = π(2 + 9√2) m². Hence the total surface area of the toy is π(2 + 9√2) m², about 46.3 m².

items.stem: From each end of a solid metal cylinder, metal was scooped out in hemispherical form of same diameter. The height of the cylinder is 10 cm and its base is of radius 4.2 cm. The rest of the cylinder is melted and converted into a cylindrical wire of 1.4 cm thickness. Find the length of the wire. Use π = 22/7
items.answer: The cylinder has radius R = 4.2 cm and height H = 10 cm, so its volume is π(4.2)² × 10 cm³. The metal scooped out is two hemispheres of the same radius, of volume 2 × (2/3)πR³ = (4/3)π(4.2)³ cm³. Metal left = π(4.2)² × 10 − (4π/3)(4.2)³ = π(4.2)²[10 − (4/3) × 4.2] = π(4.2)²(10 − 5.6) = π(4.2)² × 4.4 cm³. The wire is 1.4 cm thick, so its radius is r = 0.7 cm. Melting preserves volume, so π(0.7)²l = π(4.2)² × 4.4, giving l = (4.2 × 4.2 × 4.4)/(0.7 × 0.7) = 6 × 6 × 4.4 = 158.4. Hence the wire is 158.4 cm long.

items.stem: A milk tanker cylindrical in shape having diameter 2 m and length 4.2 m supplies milk to the two booths in the ratio of 3 : 2. One of the milk booths has cuboidal vessel having base area 3.96 sq. m. and the other has a cylindrical vessel having radius 1 m. Find the level of milk in each of the vessels. Use π = 22/7
items.answer: The tanker is a cylinder of radius R = 2/2 = 1 m and length L = 4.2 m, so it holds πR²L = (22/7) × 1 × 4.2 = 13.2 m³ of milk. Splitting this in the ratio 3 : 2 gives the first booth 13.2 × 3/5 = 7.92 m³ and the second booth 13.2 × 2/5 = 5.28 m³. The first booth’s vessel is cuboidal with base area 3.96 m², so the milk stands at 7.92/3.96 = 2 m. The second booth’s vessel is cylindrical of radius 1 m, base area π(1)² = 22/7 m², so the milk stands at 5.28 ÷ (22/7) = (5.28 × 7)/22 = 1.68 m. Hence the level of milk is 2 m in the cuboidal vessel and 1.68 m in the cylindrical vessel.

items.stem: A right triangle whose sides are 20 cm and 15 cm is made to revolve about its hypotenuse. Find the volume and the surface area of the double cone so formed. (Use π = 3.14)
items.answer: Let the right triangle ABC have legs AB = 20 cm and BC = 15 cm, so the hypotenuse is AC = √(20² + 15²) = √625 = 25 cm. Revolving about AC sweeps a double cone whose common radius is the altitude BD from B to AC. Comparing the two ways of writing the area of the triangle, (1/2) × AC × BD = (1/2) × BC × AB, so 25 × BD = 15 × 20 = 300 and BD = 12 cm. The two cones share this radius and their heights AD and CD add up to AC. Volume = (1/3)π(BD)²(AD + CD) = (1/3)π(12)²(25) = (1/3) × 3.14 × 144 × 25 = 3768 cm³. The surface of the double cone is just the two curved surfaces, with slant heights 20 cm and 15 cm: π(12)(20) + π(12)(15) = 12π(35) = 12 × 3.14 × 35 = 1318.8 cm². Hence the volume is 3768 cm³ and the surface area is 1318.8 cm².

items.stem: A solid iron pole consists of a cylinder of height 220 cm and base diameter 24 cm is surmounted by another cylinder of height 60 cm and radius 8 cm. Find the mass of the pipe, given that 1 cm3 of iron has approximately 8 g mass. (Use π = 3.14)
items.answer: The lower cylinder has radius R = 24/2 = 12 cm and height H = 220 cm; the upper cylinder has radius r = 8 cm and height h = 60 cm. Volume of the solid pole = πR²H + πr²h = 3.14 × (12)² × 220 + 3.14 × (8)² × 60 = 99475.2 + 12057.6 = 111532.8 cm³. Each cubic centimetre weighs 8 g, so the mass is 111532.8 × 8 = 892262.4 g = 892.2624 kg. Hence the mass of the pole is 892.2624 kg, about 892.26 kg.

items.stem: A solid toy is in the form of a hemisphere surmounted by a right circular cone. The height of the cone is 2 cm and the diameter of the base is 4 cm. Determine the volume of the toy. If a right circular cylinder circumscribes the toy, find the difference of the volume of the cylinder and toy. (Use π = 3.14)
items.answer: The base diameter is 4 cm, so the hemisphere and the cone share the radius r = 4/2 = 2 cm, and the cone has height h = 2 cm. Volume of toy = (2/3)πr³ + (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)πr²(2r + h) = (1/3) × 3.14 × 4 × (4 + 2) = (1/3) × 3.14 × 4 × 6 = 25.12 cm³. The circumscribing cylinder has the same radius 2 cm and a height equal to the whole toy, 2 cm of hemisphere plus 2 cm of cone, that is 4 cm, so its volume is πr²h = 3.14 × (2)² × 4 = 50.24 cm³. Difference = 50.24 − 25.12 = 25.12 cm³. Hence the toy has volume 25.12 cm³ and the cylinder exceeds it by 25.12 cm³.

items.stem: A solid wooden toy is in the form of a hemisphere surmounted by a cone of same radius. The radius of hemisphere is 3.5 cm and the total wood used in the making of toy is 166⅚ cm³. Find the height of the toy. Also find the cost of painting the hemisphere part of the toy at the rate of Rs. 10 per cm². Use π = 22/7
items.answer: The hemisphere and the cone share the radius r = 3.5 cm, and the wood used is the volume of the toy: (2/3)πr³ + (1/3)πr²h = 166⅚ = 1001/6 cm³. Writing the left side as (πr²/3)(2r + h) and clearing the fraction gives 1001 = 2πr²(2r + h) = 2 × (22/7) × (3.5)² × (7 + h) = 22 × 3.5 × (7 + h), so 91 = 2 × 3.5 × (7 + h) = 7(7 + h), i.e. 13 = 7 + h and h = 6 cm. The toy stands as tall as the cone plus the radius of the hemisphere, so its height is 6 + 3.5 = 9.5 cm. The hemispherical part painted is its curved surface, 2πr² = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 = 77 cm², costing 10 × 77 = Rs 770. Hence the toy is 9.5 cm high and painting the hemisphere costs Rs 770.

items.stem: A circus tent is in the shape of a cylinder surmounted by a conical top of same diameter. If their common diameter is 56 m, the height of cylindrical part is 6 m and the total height of the tent above the ground is 27 m, find the area of canvas used in the tent.
items.answer: The common radius is R = 56/2 = 28 m. The cylindrical wall is h = 6 m high, so the cone above it has height H = 27 − 6 = 21 m. Slant height of the cone L = √(R² + H²) = √(784 + 441) = √1225 = 35 m. Canvas covers only the curved surfaces, the wall of the cylinder and the slant of the cone, so area = 2πRh + πRL = πR(2h + L) = (22/7) × 28 × (12 + 35) = 88 × 47 = 4136. Hence 4136 m² of canvas is used in the tent.

items.stem: A heap of wheat is in the form of cone of diameter 6 m and height 3.5 m. Find its volume . How much canvas cloth is required to just cover the heap ? Use π = 22/7
items.answer: The cone has radius r = 6/2 = 3 m and height h = 3.5 m. Volume of the heap = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3) × (22/7) × 3 × 3 × 3.5 = 11 × 3 = 33 m³. To cover the heap only the curved surface is needed, so first find the slant height l = √(r² + h²) = √(3² + 3.5²) = √21.25 = 4.609 m. Canvas required = πrl = (22/7) × 3 × 4.609 = 43.45 m². Hence the heap holds 33 m³ of wheat and 43.45 m² of canvas is needed to just cover it.
